input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-based PostgreSQL/pgvector self-provisioning for Gen AI Studio

## Description

Activated when the go/no-go decision selects operator-based self-provisioning — the
outcome where the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) lands in time for
RHOAI 3.5 and provides the RHOAI-controlled operator layer. The operator self-provisions
the default PostgreSQL/pgvector instance for Gen AI Studio, following the
model-registry-operator's auto-provisioned PostgreSQL pattern (per-instance Deployment,
Service, credential Secret, and persistent storage). No custom image build or pipeline
onboarding is required: the Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image includes pgvector out of the
box, and the related-image environment variable is already present in the rhods-operator
CSV for disconnected installs. When the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL
(DSC-managed) becomes available in RHOAI 3.6, consumers can switch to the shared
connection string.

## Scope

- Implement PostgreSQL/pgvector instance provisioning in the RHOAI-controlled operator
  layer delivered by the dashboard operator modularization: Deployment, Service,
  credential Secret, and persistent storage, per playground namespace
- Use the Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image (pgvector included), resolving the image
  reference through the related-image environment variable already present in the
  rhods-operator CSV (disconnected-install compatible)
- Apply resource requests/limits referencing the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL
  sizing as the starting point, adjustable per benchmark results
- Provision one instance per playground namespace (per-namespace isolation for
  multi-tenant environments)
- Produce the PostgreSQL connection secret in the playground namespace conforming to
  the consumption contract used by the Gen AI Studio playground vector store wiring
- Design for portability: when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL (RHOAI 3.6+) is
  available, the consumer can switch to the shared connection string instead of the
  self-provisioned instance
- Owner-operator lifecycle: cleanup of the provisioned instance and its data when the
  playground is deleted

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a RAG-enabled playground in a namespace results in a running
  pgvector-enabled PostgreSQL instance provisioned by the operator, with no manual user
  steps
- The provisioned instance exposes a connection secret in the playground namespace
  matching the documented consumption contract
- Deleting the playground cleans up the provisioned PostgreSQL instance and its
  persistent data (verified by test)
- Resource requests/limits applied to the provisioned instance match the documented
  sizing reference, with any deviations recorded
- The provisioned image reference resolves via the related-image environment variable
  rather than a hardcoded registry path (disconnected-install compatible)
- Vector data in one namespace is not visible from another namespace's instance
  (per-namespace isolation verified by test)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (out-of-the-box): operator self-provisioning with zero manual steps
- HLR-3 (separate process): PostgreSQL runs as its own deployment, decoupled from the
  OGX server instance
- HLR-4 (multi-tenant scoping): one instance per namespace with isolated data
- HLR-5 (lightweight): sizing per the model-registry-operator reference

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning in the Gen AI Studio backend

## Description

Activated when the go/no-go decision selects the BFF-managed fallback — the operator
layer is not available for RHOAI 3.5 and the team keeps the zero-manual-setup
experience. The gen-ai BFF provisions the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly,
mirroring how it currently provisions guardrails infrastructure: creating the
PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and credential Secret when a playground with RAG
is configured and no suitable instance exists in the namespace. Per Staff Engineer
Input, two design concerns need explicit attention: the BFF is not an operator with a
reconciliation loop (cleanup on playground deletion, pod-restart handling, and
credential rotation need explicit design), and the implementation must be portable —
when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (RHOAI 3.6+), the BFF
should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provision.

## Scope

- Implement BFF-managed creation of the pgvector-enabled PostgreSQL Deployment,
  Service, PVC, and credential Secret when a RAG-enabled playground is configured and
  no suitable instance exists in the namespace
- Use the Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image (pgvector included), resolving the image
  reference through the related-image environment variable for disconnected installs
- Apply resource requests/limits per the model-registry-operator PostgreSQL sizing
  reference, adjustable per benchmark results
- Design lifecycle handling without a reconciliation loop: cleanup on playground
  deletion, behavior on BFF restart and PostgreSQL pod restart (no orphaned or
  duplicated instances), and a credential-rotation approach
- Design for portability: behind a configuration switch, consume an externally
  provided connection string (platform-shared database, RHOAI 3.6+) instead of
  self-provisioning
- Produce the connection secret conforming to the consumption contract used by the
  Gen AI Studio playground vector store wiring

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a playground with RAG in a namespace without a suitable existing
  PostgreSQL instance results in the BFF creating a running pgvector-enabled instance
  and its connection secret, with no manual user steps
- Deleting the playground triggers cleanup of the BFF-provisioned PostgreSQL resources
  (Deployment, Service, PVC, Secret) — verified by test
- BFF restart and PostgreSQL pod restart are handled without orphaned or duplicated
  instances — verified by test
- The self-provisioning path is behind a configuration switch that allows consuming
  an externally provided connection string instead (portability to the platform-shared
  database)
- Resource requests/limits on the created instance match the documented sizing
  reference, with any deviations recorded
- Vector data in one namespace is not visible from another namespace's instance
  (per-namespace isolation verified by test)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (out-of-the-box): BFF self-provisioning with zero manual steps
- HLR-3 (separate process): PostgreSQL runs as its own deployment, decoupled from the
  OGX server instance
- HLR-4 (multi-tenant scoping): one instance per namespace with isolated data
- HLR-5 (lightweight): sizing per the model-registry-operator reference

# Bring-your-own PostgreSQL configuration surface for Gen AI Studio RAG

## Description

Activated when the go/no-go decision selects the degraded fallback — neither
operator-based nor BFF-managed self-provisioning can ship in RHOAI 3.5. Customers
bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the playground, manually configuring
the OGXServer custom resource spec with their PostgreSQL connection details (an
explicit connection-string secret). This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in
OGX 1.0, even though the playground largely abstracts OGX from users. This outcome does
not satisfy the out-of-the-box acceptance criterion — the manual-setup limitation is a
consciously accepted decision recorded in the go/no-go decision record and must be
release-noted. The same configuration surface is also the migration path from the
default vector store to production-grade external vector databases.

## Scope

- Expose configuration for a user-provided PostgreSQL connection (connection-string
  secret) on the playground/OGXServer configuration surface
- Document the pgvector extension prerequisite on the user-provided PostgreSQL
  instance and the supported PostgreSQL versions (Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 and later
  include pgvector)
- Keep the playground abstraction intact: users configure a database connection, not
  OGX internals
- Record the accepted limitation (manual setup required for RAG in this release) in
  user-facing release notes, referencing the planned default provisioned vector store

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can supply a PostgreSQL connection secret through the configuration surface,
  and a RAG-enabled playground uses it as its vector store with no code changes
- Documentation states the pgvector prerequisite, the supported PostgreSQL versions,
  and the steps to configure the connection
- Release notes state that RAG capabilities require a user-provided PostgreSQL in this
  release (manual setup), with the default provisioned vector store referenced as the
  planned follow-up
- The same configuration surface accepts connections to external vector databases,
  demonstrating the migration path from the default store

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (migration path to production-grade vector databases): the bring-your-own
  surface is the configuration path to external databases
- HLR-3 (separate process): the user-provided PostgreSQL is decoupled from the OGX
  server instance
- HLR-1 (out-of-the-box): partial by design — this branch explicitly does not deliver
  the out-of-the-box experience; the limitation is an accepted outcome of the go/no-go
  decision

# Go/no-go decision: default vector store provisioning approach for RHOAI 3.5

## Description

Resolves the central unknown of this strategy: which provisioning approach ships the
default PostgreSQL/pgvector vector store for Gen AI Studio in RHOAI 3.5. Operator-based
self-provisioning requires a RHOAI-controlled operator layer, which is delivered by the
dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) — a hard dependency
whose delivery timing relative to the 3.5 release is not yet known. Until that is
resolved, the provisioning approach cannot be fixed. This investigation produces a

# Wire the default pgvector vector store into Gen AI Studio playground provisioning

## Description

Extends the Gen AI Studio backend (gen-ai BFF) so that playgrounds created with RAG
capabilities are configured to use the remote pgvector vector_io provider, consuming a
PostgreSQL connection secret available in the playground namespace. Today the BFF
creates OGXServer instances for the playground with application storage hardcoded to
SQLite; this epic adds the vector_io configuration on the same creation path. The
wiring is approach-invariant: the connection secret may be produced by operator-based
self-provisioning, by BFF-managed provisioning, or supplied by the user
(bring-your-own) — the consumption contract is identical, so this work proceeds
regardless of which provisioning approach is selected for RHOAI 3.5. Users perform no
manual setup for RAG workflows when a default provisioned instance is available.

## Scope

- Extend the gen-ai BFF's OGXServer creation path (llamastack_config.go) to configure
  the pgvector vector_io provider (ENABLE_PGVECTOR plus connection parameters) for
  RAG-enabled playgrounds
- Define and consume the PostgreSQL connection-secret contract in the playground
  namespace (secret name and keys), resolving credentials via the OGX `_FILE`
  secret-resolution pattern
- Preserve the existing application storage configuration (SQLite) on created
  OGXServer instances — only the vector_io configuration changes
- Preserve the configuration path to external vector databases (remote
  Milvus/Qdrant/PGVector providers remain selectable through configuration), keeping
  a migration path from the default store to production-grade vector databases
- Rollback behavior: reverting to the prior OGXServer configuration restores previous
  behavior; vector data is re-ingested on next use, so no data migration is required

## Acceptance Criteria

- A playground created with RAG enabled gets an OGXServer instance configured with
  the pgvector vector_io provider pointing at the namespace PostgreSQL connection
  secret, with no manual user configuration steps
- Playground RAG workflows (document upload, embedding, retrieval-augmented
  generation) function end-to-end against the default vector store with no loss of
  current capability — a feature-parity checklist against the inline-provider
  experience passes
- The OGXServer application storage setting is unchanged (SQLite default) when the
  vector store wiring is applied
- Replacing the default vector store with an external vector database connection is
  possible through configuration only (no code change), demonstrating the migration
  path to production-grade vector databases
- Disabling the default vector store configuration reverts playgrounds to prior
  behavior without requiring data migration

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (out-of-the-box): zero-manual-step wiring for RAG-enabled playgrounds
- HLR-2 (no loss of capability): end-to-end playground RAG parity
- HLR-3 (separate process): provider configuration targets the remote pgvector
  backend, never an inline provider
- HLR-6 (migration path): configuration-only path to external vector databases
  preserved

# Benchmark the default vector store: inline Milvus baseline versus pgvector

## Description

Captures the performance baseline of the inline Milvus provider (the capability being
replaced when inline providers are removed from the OGX distribution) and verifies
that pgvector is in the same order of magnitude on representative playground RAG
workloads. Per Staff Engineer Input this is dev-experimentation scope: strict latency
SLAs are not required, typical playground RAG usage involves small document sets, and
a flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default instance. The epic also validates
PostgreSQL resource sizing for the provisioned default instance, using the
model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL requests/limits as the starting point.

## Scope

- Define representative playground RAG workloads (small document sets; flat scan, no
  vector index) for measurement
- Capture the inline Milvus provider baseline on those workloads (latency and
  throughput)
- Measure pgvector-backed vector I/O on the same workloads through the OGX vector I/O
  API
- Record resource consumption (CPU/memory) of the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance under
  those workloads
- Compare measured consumption against the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL
  resource requests/limits as the sizing starting point and recommend adjustments
- Publish a benchmark report with results, pass/fail per metric, and the sizing
  recommendation

## Acceptance Criteria

- A benchmark report exists covering both the inline Milvus baseline and the pgvector
  measurements on identical representative workloads
- pgvector measurements are within the same order of magnitude as the inline Milvus
  baseline for each measured latency and throughput metric, with pass/fail stated per
  metric
- The report includes a resource-sizing recommendation for the default
  PostgreSQL/pgvector instance derived from measured consumption and the
  model-registry-operator reference sizing
- Any measured deviation beyond an order of magnitude is documented with a follow-up
  recommendation (index selection or sizing change) for the implementing team

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (no loss of capability): order-of-magnitude performance comparison against
  the inline Milvus baseline

  measurement and sizing recommendation
